summary.en: Haitian police have retaken the national stadium after two years of gang control, while Salvadoran missiles and ground forces struck a gang hideout, destroying the Mawozo headquarters and killing about 20 gang members, prompting the Haitian prime minister to praise President Bukele. The United Nations reported more than 1,000 people killed between July and September, and the UN chief condemned an attack that killed 47 people. Haitian security forces have intensified operations, killing a gang leader and targeting other sites. Kidnappings in the capital rose in the third quarter, and there were 193 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Haitisk politi har gjenerobret nasjonalstadion etter to år med gjengkontroll, mens salvadoranske missiler og bakkestyrker angrep et gjengskjul, ødela Mawozo-hovedkvarteret og drepte omtrent 20 gjengmedlemmer, noe som fikk den haitiske statsministeren til å rose president Bukele. FN rapporterte at mer enn 1 000 personer ble drept mellom juli og september, og FN-sjefen fordømte et angrep som drepte 47 personer. Haitiske sikkerhetsstyrker har intensivert operasjonene, drept en gjengleder og rettet seg mot andre steder. Kidnappinger i hovedstaden økte i tredje kvartal, og det var 193 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
